title: Neurological manifestations of Long Covid-19 in Germany - an observational study (NEURO LC-19 DE)
summary: According to current knowledge, about 10-20% of all COVID-19 patients suffer from a post-COVID-19 syndrome.  Neurological symptoms in particular are associated with enormous losses in the quality of life of the affected patients and with drastic restrictions in their participation in social and professional life. There is therefore need to collect robust and well phenotyped clinical data on neurological and neuropsychological consequences of COVID-19.
conditions: U09.9! Post-Covid 19 condition: intended for cases in which the association of a current condition classified elsewhere with a previous coronavirus disease should be coded.

interventions.name: Patients who present themselves due to neurological PCS manifestations in the post-COVID-19 outpatient clinic of the Clinic and Polyclinic for Neurology and in the post-COVID network of the Charité as well as in the interdispensary neuro-PCS consultation of the UK Bonn and who would like to particip

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria (PCS patients with cognitive deficits):
- PCS according to NICE guidelines.
- Confirmation of the initial acute infection by positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR result or serological detection of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid antibodies, or positive SARS-CoV-2 rapid antigen test with medical certificate for infections from 2024 onwards
- Leading cognitive deficits in the context of the PCS

Inclusion criteria (PCS patients without cognitive deficits):
- PCS according to NICE guidelines.
- Confirmation of the initial acute infection by positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR result or serological detection of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid antibodies, or positive SARS-CoV-2 rapid antigen test with medical certificate for infections from 2024 onwards
- Absence of cognitive deficits as a result of COVID-19

Inclusion criteria (control subjects without PCS):
- Absence of PCS according to NICE guidelines.
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute COVID-19 disease (<4 weeks).
- For PCS patients: Absence of confirmation of acute infection by PCR or specific serology or rapid antigen test with medical certificate
- Present symptoms in PCS patients are more likely to be explained by other other diagnosis
- Pregnancy
- Breastfeeding
- Insufficient knowledge of German
- Participation in an AMG study
- beinig under care 
- not being able to give consent
